original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-injective-map-simplicial-sets}
Let $f : U \to V$ be a morphism of simplicial sets.
Suppose that (a) the image of every nondegenerate simplex of
$U$ is a nondegenerate simplex of $V$ and (b) the restriction
of $f$ to a map from the set of nondegenerate simplices of $U$
to the set of nondegenerate simplices of $V$ is injective.
Then $f_n$ is injective for all $n$.
Same holds with ``injective'' replaced by
``surjective'' or ``bijective''.
hold_reason: Pinned lemma says injectivity on nondegenerate simplices under nondegenerate-image preservation yields levelwise injectivity, and analogous statements replace injective with surjective and bijective in both premises and results. Proposed structured hypotheses hardcode the injectivity premise, while conclusions claim the surjectivity and bijectivity versions without separately recording their changed premises. This is unsafe for direction-aware hypothesis searches.
proposed_correction: Represent three separate conditional cases (injective, surjective, bijective), always keeping the nondegeneracy-preservation requirement and matching each premise to its same-type conclusion; independently re-review.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-simplicial-set-n-skel-sub}
Let $U$ be a simplicial set.
Let $n \geq 0$ be an integer.
The rule
$$
U'_m = \bigcup\nolimits_{\varphi : [m] \to [i], \ i\leq n} \Im(U(\varphi))
$$
defines a sub simplicial set $U' \subset U$ with
$U'_i = U_i$ for $i \leq n$.
Moreover, all $m$-simplices of $U'$ are degenerate for
all $m > n$.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-injective-map-simplicial-abelian}
\begin{slogan}
The Dold-Kan normalization functor reflects
injectivity, surjectivity, and isomorphy.
\end{slogan}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $f : U \to V$ be a morphism of
simplicial objects of $\mathcal{A}$.
If the induced morphisms $N(f)_i : N(U)_i \to N(V)_i$
are injective for all $i$, then $f_i$ is
injective for all $i$. Same holds with ``injective'' replaced
with ``surjective'', or ``isomorphism''.
hold_reason: The pinned normalization-reflection lemma has injectivity, surjectivity and isomorphism variants under correspondingly different hypotheses on N(f)_i. The proposal's structured hypothesis records only injectivity while its conclusion adds the other two variants, and the standalone displayed statement contains the source-only \begin{slogan}...\end{slogan} environment.
proposed_correction: Remove the slogan and encode each of the three corresponding conditions on N(f) as a separate conditional case with the matching conclusion on f, preserving category A and all degrees i; independent review.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-N-d-in-N}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $U$ be a simplicial object in $\mathcal{A}$.
Let $N(U_m)$ as in Lemma \ref{lemma-splitting-abelian-category} above.
Then $d^m_m(N(U_m)) \subset N(U_{m - 1})$.

final_content.statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $U$ be a simplicial object in $\mathcal{A}$.
For every \(m\geq 1\), define \(N(U_m)=\bigcap_{i=0}^{m-1}\ker(d_i^m)\), and set \(N(U_0)=U_0\).
Then $d^m_m(N(U_m)) \subset N(U_{m - 1})$.
hypotheses: Let A be an abelian category and U a simplicial object of A; for each m set N(U_m)=intersection of ker d_i^m over 0≤i<m, with N(U_0)=U_0.
conclusions: For each m≥1, the last face map d_m^m carries N(U_m) into N(U_{m-1}).

semantic_review_note: The pinned statement cites prior normalization splitting; the proposal explicitly sets N(U_m)=intersection of kernels of faces i<m, including N(U_0)=U_0. The last face d_m maps N(U_m) to N(U_{m-1}), with m≥1 and appropriate index scope.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-simplicial-abelian-n-skel-sub}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
Let $U$ be a simplicial object of $\mathcal{A}$.
Let $n \geq 0$ be an integer.
The rule
$$
U'_m = \sum\nolimits_{\varphi : [m] \to [i], \ i\leq n} \Im(U(\varphi))
$$
defines a sub simplicial object $U' \subset U$ with $U'_i = U_i$
for $i \leq n$.
Moreover, $N(U'_m) = 0$ for all $m > n$.
